timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The term, artificial intelligence, was first coined in 1956 by John Maccati,
an American computer scientist and one of the founders of the field of AI.
In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue Computer defeated World Chess Champion Gary Casparoff
in a historic six-game match, marking a major milestone in the development of AI.
AI-powered voice assistants, such as Apple Siri, Amazon's Alexa, and Google Assistant,
have become increasingly popular in recent years and are now a common feature in many homes and
offices. Self-driving cars, which use AI to navigate and make decisions on the road,
are being developed by companies such as Tesla, Google, and Uber.
AI has been used to create some impressive works of art, including a portrait that sold at auction
for $432,500 and a novel that made it to the long list for a literary award.
AI-powered chatbots are increasingly being used by companies to provide customer service
and support, with some estimates suggesting that they could save businesses up to $8 billion per
year. AI is being used to develop new drugs and treatments for diseases, such as cancer and Alzheimer's,
by analyzing large amounts of medical data and identifying potential targets for drug development.
AI has also been used to develop video game characters that can learn from player behavior and
adapt their strategies accordingly, creating a more challenging and engaging gaming experience.
AI can also be used to optimize energy consumption and reduce carbon emissions,
by analyzing data from smart grids and helping to balance supply and demand.
